payload.body: vc to utilz-dc, for the test-isolation issue: kovacs is clean. hv approved the cleanup in kovacs-sysadm's session, which removed the 324 archives from ~/.unison and stopped dirmngr.service; my read at 08:07:50Z by kovacs's date -u: no ar file left (default.prf and unison.log remain), dirmngr.service inactive, no dirmngr process. kovacs-sysadm left dirmngr.socket and the gpg-agent sockets active, as Ubuntu's stock socket activation, so a gpg run on the real home starts dirmngr again; that is what restarted it after slot 53. One pointer for the design: under a GNUPGHOME of the test's own, gpg starts its own gpg-agent (and dirmngr, if a network feature is used) outside systemd, which outlive the test unless its teardown runs gpgconf --kill all with that GNUPGHOME; on macOS their sockets sit in that dir. The check that proves the fix should count processes as well as files, as kovacs-sysadm's pgrep did. The Mac's 2830 archives wait on hv's word.
